subject: /tmp/opensip-implementation/m1-ts-runtime-subject-02
verdictScope: Accepts only the trial algorithms in exact-json.ts, schema.ts and patterns.ts for later integration review. It does not accept generated product integration, a public API, a production Rust dependency (regress is a probe only), build/tool selection, or M1/release qualification. Author test counts were not treated as approval: every conclusion below rests on my own reruns and independent probes.

R1.basis: The runtime no longer applies native JS regex semantics to pinned patterns. It looks each pattern up in an exact 66-entry table and refuses anything else. Six entries are rewritten: an unescaped dot outside a class becomes [^\n], and a bare $ becomes (?=\n?(?![\s\S])). Everything else is unchanged. These are exactly Python re semantics without DOTALL or MULTILINE, and jsonschema 4.25.1 _keywords.pattern uses re.search. I checked the remaining constructs by hand: ASCII classes, \u escapes, [\s\S] only as a pair, (?!, (?:, bounded quantifiers, and ^ without the m flag. They have the same language in both engines. Independent evidence: 26,790,060 exhaustive small-alphabet and structured-insertion comparisons with 0 mismatches. A mutation control running the unmapped sources on the same harness gives 185,478 mismatches, so the harness does detect divergence. My review-01 corpus of 68,640 rows now gives 0 mismatches, and the end-to-end path booleans agree. The Rust regress probe rerun on my copy gives 0 of 39,336 mismatches.

R2.basis: matches() now evaluates parseExact(canonical(value)) (schema.ts:114). canonical() requires Array.prototype (exact-json.ts:117). My review-01 bypasses are all refused or now report the correct result: a custom array prototype and an Array subclass throw PLAIN_ARRAY_REQUIRED; a Proxy get trap and a Proxy returning a fake every() both return false. Arrays and objects from another vm realm are refused, and local and growable SharedArrayBuffer views are refused. Proxy effects are explicitly outside the inert-input contract. Even a Proxy that lies in its descriptors yields a snapshot that is consistent with itself.

priorFindings.A1: RESOLVED: 18,000 random arrays across 12 annotations, evaluated both bare and under not (36,000 evaluations) against canonical.py exact_order, 0 mismatches. The review-01 set of 2680 real-node cases gives 0 mismatches.
priorFindings.A2: RESOLVED for the selected vocabulary. Additional malformations are refused with SchemaError: duplicate type entries, a foreign nested $id or $schema, an unprofiled patternProperties key, a non-object properties, an extra key in an order annotation, and a structurally duplicate enum. Unreferenced $defs are not validated, by design.
priorFindings.A3: CARRIED LIMITATION, confirmed: a fragment-less self $ref still yields ShapeLimit.
priorFindings.A4: RESOLVED: schema-probe.mjs runs metadata-reference.py and compares; 43 of 43 match.
priorFindings.A5: CARRIED LIMITATION: a 4 MiB object with the snapshot takes 523 ms; there is still no hard time budget.

patternProfileAssessment.decision: ACCEPTABLE as a scoped finite compatibility mapping for exactly these 66 source patterns in the 28 pinned metadata-v2 documents. Root assent is still required before product integration.
grounds: Product identity-and-evidence.md section 2 (lines 64-76) explicitly treats a bare trailing $ as admitting a final LF (exec1_<hex>\n) and treats (?![\s\S]) as the exact end guard. Preserving reference $ semantics is therefore consistent with the documented product reading, not an invention.
The mapping preserves the raw schema bytes and the historical evidence, and refuses unknown patterns. It is not a general Python re port.

Regenerating pattern-profile.py in a separate copy reproduces pattern-profile.json, patterns.ts and pattern-cases.json byte-for-byte. Its sources equal metadata-v2 sources.json, and its 66 patterns are the same set I extracted in review-01.
Semantic equivalence was established by construct analysis and by an exhaustive differential whose sensitivity was checked by mutation (see R1).
conditions: Any changed source pattern, added pattern or new engine requires regenerating the table, an independent differential and review, as PROFILE.md states.

The translator in pattern-profile.py is a character scanner, not a regex parser. Cases such as ] as the first class member, inline flags and lookbehind are not handled. It is acceptable only because its output is frozen and reviewed for these 66 inputs.
Shape acceptance is never filesystem or identity authority (ADV-1, ADV-2).

advisories.title: Retained CanonicalPath pattern admits LF-separated parent traversal in every engine
advisories.detail:
Both the reference and TS accept 'a
/../../etc/passwd', 'a
/..' and 'a
/../x' as evidence-schemas:v2#/$defs/CanonicalPath, because the lookahead's .* / [^
]* cannot cross LF. The runtime reproduces this faithfully and PROFILE.md discloses it. native-evidence.md:644 separates CanonicalPath from the canonical relative directory grammar and does not claim it is traversal-free. The LogicalPath variants refuse these inputs. Owner obligation: host path and custody admission must check components independently, and a successor schema should use [\s\S] or (?![\s\S]). This is not a runtime defect.

advisories.title: Unescaped dots in the security.repo-execution-grant(s).v2 identity patterns
advisories.detail: Faithful to the reference: both engines accept 'securityXrepo-execution-grantXv2:<64 hex>', and the grants variant accepts U+2028 and / as separators. These patterns appear in native-evidence.schemas.v2.json, invocation-record.schema.json and test-execution.schema.json. Semantic owners must compare the exact digest domain prefix, and a successor schema should escape the dots.

advisories.title: SharedArrayBuffer refusal is realm-local
advisories.detail: parseExact(new Uint8Array(sabFromAnotherVmRealm)) is accepted, because raw.buffer instanceof SharedArrayBuffer is false. It is same-thread and inside the declared trusted-builtins scope, so the risk is low. A brand check (Object.prototype.toString.call(raw.buffer) === '[object SharedArrayBuffer]') would close it. Resizable non-shared ArrayBuffer and Buffer inputs are accepted, which is correct.

advisories.title: Rust probe log provenance
advisories.detail: The frozen rust-pattern-check.log records a run from /tmp/opensip-implementation/m1-ts-runtime-trial-02, not from the frozen subject path. I reran cargo --locked --offline against my copy: 0 of 39,336 mismatches. With the probe's workspace configuration, cargo placed target/ at /tmp/opensip-implementation/m1-ts-runtime-review-02/target, which is inside the permitted write area.

advisories.title: Carried A3/A5 limitations remain integration inputs
advisories.detail: A non-productive $ref cycle is reported as ShapeLimit, not SchemaError. canonical, snapshot and regex work is not metered, and there is no wall-clock or regex backtracking budget. Integration must choose the limits and host timeouts.

limitations: The Python reference and the metadata-v2 adapter are comparators whose selection is the root's decision; this review accepts the profile only as a faithful compatibility mapping, not as the ideal pattern grammar.
The exhaustive alphabet has 13 symbols and strings up to length 5, plus structured insertions. Equivalence beyond that rests on construct analysis of the frozen 66 patterns.
Regress was run only as a conformance probe. Its production suitability, supply chain and performance were not evaluated.
No coverage-guided lexer fuzzing, no backtracking or wall-clock analysis, and no non-Node runtimes.
Only 110 of 589 refs have valid-case witnesses in the harvested data; the 589-entrypoint selection was taken as given.
Proxy, concurrent-mutation and untrusted-builtin inputs are outside the declared contract and were probed only for snapshot consistency.
